summary: Durable tool recovery replayed a persisted replay:"safe" effect without re-checking the tool declaration it resolves at reopen. A tool that disappeared from the current configuration was passed to the effect boundary as undefined and turned into a bogus TypeError result (plus a recovery tool_start), and a tool whose declaration had become replay:"never" was re-executed anyway. Recovery now replays only when the persisted intent and the current declaration are both safe and the batch is not cancelled; every other case settles as interrupted with the durable progress checkpoint preserved, and a missing tool never reaches the effect boundary.

changes.description: recoverToolInvocation guards the replay branch with the current declaration: tool !== undefined (missing declaration falls through to the interrupted settlement) and tool.replay === "safe" (a downgraded declaration cannot repeat the effect). Both are combined with the persisted call.replay === "safe" and !cancelled, so only both-safe, non-cancelled calls replay.

citations.claim: recoverToolInvocation is the recovery entry point for an effect_pending tool call; the fixed guard is line 529 and the interrupted settlement fallback is the tail of the function (readCheckpoint + interruptedOutcome + publishToolOutcome).
interruptedOutcome keeps the durable checkpoint content/details/usage and appends the INTERRUPTION_MARKER text; this is the settlement the regression asserts on.
clearReplayCheckpoint (replay intent publication) is only reached from the replay branch, so a guarded-out call no longer clears the durable checkpoint before deciding.
performToolInvocation is the effect boundary: prepare/replay hands it the resolved declaration, so an undefined declaration would reach executeToolCall and fail there under the original code.
runTools builds toolsByName from the current lane configuration filtered by the persisted activeToolNames, i.e. exactly the current declaration set recovery must re-check.
executeToolCall dereferences call.tool.execute inside its try block, which is why a missing declaration surfaced as a TypeError-derived error result instead of an interruption.

The experimental pico3 kernel already encodes the intended rule on recovery (`if (cp.replay !== "safe" || (declaration.replay ?? "unsafe") !== "safe")` and a separate missing-declaration branch); the drive runtime is the implementation that violated it.

validation.notes: The regression loads the real production modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs createGraph (drive/tools.ts plus the lane, restore, tool-placement, progress, execution and session modules it links against) and fakes only the boundary: the pi-ai argument validator, uuidv7, and the chord context helpers. It rebuilds a reopened durable tool batch exactly as the kernel persists it (assistant message with tool-call blocks, operation meta/state with effect_pending calls, persisted operationToolArgs and pendingToolOutput checkpoints) and runs runTools on it. Scenarios: (1) persisted replay:"safe" with the declaration gone -> asserts the tool never runs, no recovery tool_start is emitted, and the result carries the durable snapshot 'durable partial' plus the interruption marker and its details; (2) declaration downgraded to replay:"never" -> same interrupted settlement, zero executions; (3) declaration with no replay field (default not safe) -> interrupted with marker only and no invented details; (4) control: both policies safe -> the effect replays exactly once with the persisted arguments and publishes the real result with one recovery tool_start; (5) persisted replay:"never" with a now-safe declaration -> interrupted, because the durable policy cannot be upgraded; (6) mixed batch (missing + downgraded) -> both settle interrupted and are placed in source order. Verified both directions: with the fix the script exits 0, and with the original line `if (!cancelled && call.replay === "safe")` restored it exits 1 with AssertionError 'missing declaration: the result must report an interrupted tool execution, got: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'execute\')'; a partial fix that only guards the missing declaration also fails it ('declaration downgraded to never: the tool effect ran even though the call must not replay'). Runtime is ~0.15s, no dependencies or network. Limitation: node_modules is absent in this checkout, so the repository's vitest suite and `npm run check` (tsc/biome) could not be run; the module graph is instead parsed and evaluated by Node 24 type stripping, which validates the edited file's syntax, and the affected existing vitest case (packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-tools.test.ts, 'safe-replays persisted arguments and memos while interrupting unsafe effects') was reviewed by hand: its safe tool declares replay:"safe" and its unsafe one replay:"never", so both its expectations still hold.
